questions.question: According to Lowry-Brønsted, an acid is a:
A conjugate acid-base pair consists of two species that differ by exactly:
When nitric acid donates a proton to water, the conjugate base formed from the acid is:
An ampholyte is a substance that:
options: Can act as either an acid or a base, like water and the hydrogen carbonate ion

subtopics.title: Strong, Weak, Concentrated, Dilute — and K a

questions.question: A STRONG acid is one that:
Double-strength kitchen vinegar is best described as:
A very small Ka value, like ethanoic acid's ten to the minus five, indicates:
options: A weak acid — the ionisation equilibrium lies far toward the intact molecules

questions.question: At equal concentration, a strong acid differs measurably from a weak one by having:
options: A higher pH and slower reactions
The same pH but better conductivity
A lower pH, better conductivity, and faster reaction with magnesium

subtopics.title: pH, K w and the Calculations

questions.question: Nitric acid of concentration 0,001 mol·dm⁻³ ionises completely. Its pH is:
Sulfuric acid of concentration 0,005 mol·dm⁻³ (diprotic, fully ionised) has a pH of:
Potassium hydroxide of concentration 0,01 mol·dm⁻³: using Kw = 10⁻¹⁴, its pH is:
Ethanoic acid at 0,001 mol·dm⁻³ has a pH around 3,9 rather than 3 because:
options: It donates two protons per molecule
Kw does not apply to weak acids
The logarithm works differently for organic acids
Only a fraction of its molecules ionise, so the hydronium concentration is below 0,001

subtopics.title: Titrations, Indicators and the pH of Salts

questions.question: 30 cm³ of KOH is exactly neutralised by 15 cm³ of 0,2 mol·dm⁻³ nitric acid (1:1 ratio). The KOH concentration is:
The equivalence point of a titration is the moment when:
options: Acid and base have reacted in the exact mole ratio of the balanced equation

questions.question: At equivalence in a weak-acid/strong-base titration, the solution is basic because the salt's anion:
options: Is a spectator with no effect
Accepts protons from water, releasing hydroxide ions

questions.question: Titrating ammonia with hydrochloric acid, the fitting indicator is:
options: Methyl orange — the ammonium salt makes equivalence acidic, below 7

questions.question: In the parcel picture, the parcel passed in every acid-base reaction is:
After an acid hands over its proton, the species left behind is:
options: Its conjugate base — the same species one proton lighter

questions.question: Water gives a proton to ammonia but takes one from nitric acid. This makes water:
options: An ampholyte — able to give or take depending on its partner

questions.question: In the cordial picture, the amount of syrup poured into the glass stands for:
The syrup that dissolves instantly and completely stands for:
options: A strong acid — every molecule splits and donates its proton

questions.question: Pool-test drops containing a trace of fully ionised hydrochloric acid are:
Ka puts a number on:
options: The amount of acid dissolved per volume
The willingness to ionise — strength, not concentration

subtopics.title: The Ladder of Tens and the Exact Balance

questions.question: A river's pH falls from 6 to 4. Its hydronium concentration has:
Pure water sits at pH 7 because:
options: It contains no ions at all
It holds equal, tiny concentrations of hydronium and hydroxide
Kw equals zero for pure water

questions.question: In a titration, the indicator's job is to:
options: Change colour at the pH of the equivalence point

questions.question: Vinegar neutralised by caustic soda leaves a solution at equivalence that is:
options: Slightly basic — the salt takes after its stronger parent
